correctness.rationale: At alpha=-a the entire power-mean inequality is exactly nonnegative second difference of h_a(k)=product_{j=0}^rho(k+j)^a. First-triple root is unique by F(0)=0,Fprime(0)<0,Fsecond>0. f=S2/S1^2 is strictly decreasing by Cauchy-Schwarz; R is its positive sliding-window average with Rprime<0. Therefore the secant slope has at most one negative-to-positive turn, and its first integer rise forces all subsequent rises. Separate second-derivative comparisons prove 1/(rho+1)<a_rho<b_rho. The numerical script passed 6049 checks, not an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: A recent paper derives variance/entropy/concentration conclusions for alpha-concave discrete laws and supplies only a conservative parameter for the basic Yule-Simon heavy-tail example. This theorem answers the natural sharp index classification over every integer shape; the first triple uniquely governs infinitely many constraints, and strict improvement of the admissible alpha is relevant for applying alpha-parameterized bounds. No downstream optimal inequality is asserted.
